graphEvents.label: lighthouse_audit is a real, locally registered MCP tool

label: Yes: chrome-devtools-mcp exposes lighthouse_audit as a first-class Debugging tool for accessibility/SEO/best practices/agentic browsing; full reports saved to disk; performance excluded.

The tool is locally registered: the 2026-07-16 list_tools fixture shows lighthouse_audit, performance_start/stop_trace, performance_analyze_insight and take_memory_snapshot on BOTH chrome_devtools_1 and chrome_devtools_2 (29 tools each).

The feature-catalog gap is a granularity artifact: 30 features enumerate CLI features and MCP invocation patterns, not the 26/29 MCP tool names, and the catalog explicitly requires per-session discovery instead of freezing names.

The router was right and needs no keyword rewrite: lighthouse is a CHROME_DEVTOOLS intent keyword in ROUTER.md, hub-router.json, mode-registry.json and graph-metadata.json, and is advertised as runnable intent at ROUTER.md:49-53.

Scope split: lighthouse_audit excludes performance; Core Web Vitals and traces come from performance_start_trace / performance_stop_trace / performance_analyze_insight, so KQ1 and the new hub should carry two rows, not one.

Lighthouse is fallback-lane only: the bdg CLI feature catalog lists raw CDP, HAR export and example scripts but no Lighthouse command; 004/005 should add a Lighthouse + performance-trace leaf so the advertised intent has a describing leaf.

Do not freeze a tool count: the catalog says 26 exposed tools, the 2026-07-16 fixture shows 29 per instance, and the current upstream reference is larger and flag-gated; rediscover the inventory each session.
A router-advertised capability must have either a describing packet leaf or a registered tool inventory entry; a feature-catalog omission alone does not disprove capability.

direction: Treat the missing catalog row as proof that Lighthouse is unavailable
